concerns.text: T067 instructs validating contract conformance 'against the schemas in specs/001-transferability-of-dft-d3-dispersion-to-/contracts/', but plan.md's Project Structure places all feature artifacts under 'specs/PROJ-735-transferability-of-dft-d3-dispersion-to-/'. The implementer cannot deterministically resolve which directory to validate against; the verification step may fail or validate the wrong path. Pick one canonical contracts path and use it consistently.

Canonical artifact paths are inconsistent within tasks.md: T065 cites 'data/derived/raw_energies.csv' and 'data/derived/scaling_factor.txt', while the Completed-work section lists 'scaling_factor.txt' with no data/derived/ prefix; T068 references 'data/derived/raw_energies.csv, scaling_factor.txt, correlation_results.csv' mixing prefixed and bare names in one list. An implementer cannot deterministically locate the files to cite/link. Normalize all derived-artifact paths (e.g., consistently 'data/derived/<name>').

T067's verification records 'commands, exit codes, and artifact checksums' but SC-005 also requires evidence of ≤6 h runtime and ≤7 GB RAM. As written, the task's verification is executable but produces no evidence for the resource limits. Add a concrete measurement step (e.g., '/usr/bin/time -v' wrapper or CI job summary recording wall time and peak RSS) recorded in the same 'Reproducibility Check' section.

T065's verification 'cites the actual numbers from data/derived/raw_energies.csv and scaling_factor.txt — no hand-typed or invented values' is not mechanically checkable as stated. Make it concrete: e.g., the Calibration Procedure section's numbers must be generated by a script (per SSoT Principle IV) or the verification must name a diff/trace check against the derived files.
